newsitem.title: CANADA: Caledonia reports Zambia cobalt tonnages.
newsitem.headline: Caledonia reports Zambia cobalt tonnages.

text.p: Caledonia Mining Corp said on Monday it had completed initial tonnage and grade estimates for the Nama Anomaly C cobalt discovery in Zambia.
An initial resource of 64 million tonnes at 0.034 percent cobalt equivalent has been determined, using a 0.015 percent cobalt equivalent cutoff, the company said in a release.
Using a 0.03 percent cobalt equivalent, the resource is 29 million tonnes at 0.048 percent cobalt equivalent, Caledonia said.
The deposit remains open in all directions.
Caledonia said the estimates were done by Toronto-based Watts, Griffis and McOuat Ltd, Consulting Geologists and Engineers.
The tonnages are in addition to initial resources announced last month from Caledonia's Anomaly A area 11 kilometres southeast of Anomaly C.

The inferred mineral resource at Anomaly A consists of 16.3 million tonnes at 0.049 percent cobalt equivalent, using a 0.015 percent cutoff or 7.6 million tonnes at 0.081 percent cobalt equivalent using a 0.03 percent cutoff.
Over 99 percent of the cobalt equivalent comes from cobalt, while the rest comes from copper, the company said.
